questions.text: Define IT and IT infrastructure. Explain the components of IT infrastructure with examples of each component.

sub_parts.text: Explain the components of IT infrastructure with examples of each component.

marking_scheme.point: Defines Information Technology (IT) with reference to its purpose (process, store, exchange data) and scope (hardware, software, services).
Defines IT Infrastructure as the foundational framework of physical/virtual resources supporting the IT environment.
Explains Hardware components (physical devices for processing/storage/transmission) with relevant examples (e.g., servers, client devices, storage devices).
Explains Software components (programs/applications for tasks, management, interaction) with relevant examples (e.g., OS, enterprise apps, DBMS).
Explains Networking components (connecting resources for communication) with relevant examples (e.g., routers, switches, firewalls, cabling, protocols).
Explains Data Management components (systems/processes for storing, organizing, protecting data) with relevant examples (e.g., database systems, SAN/NAS, backup/recovery systems).

questions.text: How are information systems transforming modern business and how do they support globalization?

marking_scheme.point: Explains that IS automate processes and improve efficiency (e.g., ERP).
States that IS enhance decision-making through data analytics/BI.
Discusses how IS improve customer experience/engagement (e.g., CRM, e-commerce).
Mentions how IS enable new business models (e.g., digital platforms, sharing economy).
Highlights the role of IS in improving global communication and coordination.
Explains how IS expand market reach through e-commerce and digital presence.
Describes how IS streamline global supply chain management.
Notes that IS facilitate standardization and integration of global operations.

questions.text: What is a business process? Briefly explain about examples of business process for functional areas of the business.

marking_scheme.point: Defines a business process as a collection of related activities/tasks producing a service/product for a customer/market, achieving a goal, and often crossing departmental boundaries.
Provides an example of a business process for Sales & Marketing (e.g., Order-to-Cash) and briefly explains it.
Provides an example of a business process for Manufacturing/Production (e.g., Production Planning) and briefly explains it.
Provides an example of a business process for Finance & Accounting (e.g., Accounts Payable or Payroll Processing) and briefly explains it.

Provides an example of a business process for Human Resources (e.g., Recruitment & Onboarding) and briefly explains it. (An example from R&D can be accepted here as an optional alternative for a functional area.)

questions.text: Define value chain model and explain the activities associated to the value chain model.

marking_scheme.point: Defines Value Chain Model, mentioning Porter and its purpose of identifying competitive advantage.
States the two main categories of activities: Primary Activities and Support Activities.
Explains the five Primary Activities (Inbound Logistics, Operations, Outbound Logistics, Marketing & Sales, Service), with a brief description for each. (0.6 marks per activity explanation)
Explains the four Support Activities (Firm Infrastructure, Human Resource Management, Technology Development, Procurement), with a brief description for each. (0.5 marks per activity explanation)

questions.text: "Using a database system helps to improve business performance". Explain.

marking_scheme.point: Explains how databases improve data organization and consistency, reducing redundancy and errors.
Explains how databases enhance data accessibility, enabling timely and informed decision-making.
Explains how databases ensure better data integrity and security, protecting information.
Explains how databases facilitate reporting, analytics, and improve operational efficiency.

questions.text: Define vulnerability. Briefly write about tools and techniques used for safeguarding organizational information resources.

marking_scheme.point: Defines vulnerability as a weakness/flaw that can be exploited by a threat
States Access Control Systems as a safeguarding tool and explains its purpose (authentication/authorization)
States Encryption as a safeguarding tool and explains its purpose (data confidentiality for data at rest/in transit)
States Firewalls as a safeguarding tool and explains its purpose (network traffic filtering/barrier)
States Intrusion Detection/Prevention Systems (IDPS) as a safeguarding tool and explains its purpose (monitoring/blocking malicious activity)
States Antivirus and Anti-malware Software as a safeguarding tool and explains its purpose (detecting/removing malicious software)
States Security Policies and Employee Training as a safeguarding technique and explains its purpose (guidelines/education for human factors)

questions.text: Write short notes on Any TWO: (a) SISP (b) Components of DSS (c) Quality Information System

Mentions it involves analyzing business strategy and current IS capabilities (or similar key step).
States the outcome is an IT plan that guides IS development.
Briefly defines a DSS.
Identifies and describes the Data Management Subsystem (or Data Subsystem).
Identifies and describes the Model Management Subsystem (or Model Subsystem).
Identifies and describes the User Interface Subsystem (or Dialogue System).
Defines a Quality Information System as one that provides accurate, timely, and relevant information.

Explains the characteristic of Relevance and/or Completeness.
